title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative
description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week.  
 To Participate : RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set! 
 Requirements: 
 
 Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate. 
 Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this  link . 
 Once certified, email your certification to  foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org  to confirm your eligibility to participate. 
 
 Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation! *Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: Movie Screening of Politics is a Mother: Raising Hell is Part of the Job
location: College of Coms and Media: Presentation Hall
description:
At 79 years old, New Jersey Senator Loretta Weinberg wasn’t slowing down—she was at the height of her influence and just getting started. 
 Affectionately known as the “Feisty Grandma,” the former Senate majority leader built a reputation for challenging powerful figures, standing up for what she believed in, and refusing to stay quiet. She turned New Jersey politics upside down when she helped uncover the infamous Bridgegate scandal, contributing to Governor Chris Christie’s dramatic fall from power and proving that determination can shake even the strongest political establishment. 
 But behind the headlines, heated debates, and political victories is a warm and wonderfully complicated mother-daughter story. Told through that personal lens,  Politics Is a Mother: Raising Hell Is Part of the Job  offers a funny, heartfelt, and revealing look at the woman behind the public figure. It explores how family shaped Weinberg’s political life—and how politics became part of the family. 
 Full of humor, heart, history, and a healthy dose of hell-raising, this story shows why the political is always personal. It also proves that an “adorable grandmother” can be a fearless advocate, a relentless reformer, and one of the most important and influential politicians of our time.

title: Pride and Progress: Celebrating LGBTQ+ and Disability Journeys
description:
Join Advocacy and Outreach for our 3rd Annual LGBTQ+ and Disability History and Awareness Month Flag Raising and Reception — a joyful celebration of identity, resilience, and community! 
 Pride and Progress brings together students, faculty, and staff to honor the rich histories and vibrant futures of LGBTQ+ and disability communities. Enjoy an inspiring flag-raising ceremony featuring an energetic MC, powerful speakers, and a special live performance you won’t want to miss. 
 This year's theme is "The World Works Better With Us: Celebrating the valuable contributions of queer and disabled folks in professional and learning spaces while collectively advocating for continued respect, inclusion, and empowerment". 
 Come as you are, bring your friends, and help us raise our voices (and our flags!) in honor of progress, pride, and community power. 
 This event is hosted by Advocacy & Outreach in collaboration with the Office of Community Resilience and Officer Wellness, GSWS, Student Health Center, Inclusive Excellence, Disability Resource Center, Health Promotion, CAPS, Garden State Equality, Queer Employee Network, and Disability Caucus.

title: Fall Symposium: Reclaiming the Narrative
description:
In celebration of Archives Month, University Libraries will highlight how primary source materials can bring marginalized stories to the center of education, advocacy, and community engagement. Dr. Melissa Benbow Flowers, Scholar‑in‑Residence at Sprague Library (2025–2026), in collaboration with Bloomfield College, will host a symposium exploring how working‑class histories and undertold stories in New Jersey are researched, interpreted, and shared with the public. The program will bring together scholars, students, museum professionals, and public historians whose work focuses on labor, domestic work, immigration, race, and community change—particularly as these histories are communicated through museums, historic sites, archives, and public‑facing scholarship. Registration is free and open to students, faculty, staff, and members of the public—but limited!  Registration closes September 18 . 
 Register now for in-person attendance. 
   
 You can also attend virtually! 
 Here are the Zoom registration links:  
   
 Session 1, 9:30AM-11AM: Centering Indigenous Histories: Roundtable and Discussion  https://montclair.zoom.us/ meeting/register/ mFKcJC2GTymrGXonBJVN0Q Session 2, 11:00AM - 12:00PM: Presentation: "Unveiled: The Narratives of a Predominantly Black Institution" https://montclair.zoom.us/ meeting/register/6u_ omu0kQxKlsOolZecQzQ Lunch Conversation,  12:15PM-1:30PM: Centering Place and People with the New Jersey Black Heritage Trail  https://montclair.zoom.us/ meeting/register/ OjdkxfUPRaacoj3h_1DgRQ Session 3: 1:30PM - 3:30PM: Doing the Work of Public History in Museums and Community Organizations: Panel and Breakout Discussion  https://montclair.zoom.us/ meeting/register/ pLTOaJakSGu3FCq8kgxCFw

title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative
description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week.  
 To Participate : RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set! 
 Requirements: 
 
 Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate. 
 Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this  link . 
 Once certified, email your certification to  foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org  to confirm your eligibility to participate. 
 
 Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation! *Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: 3rd Annual Power of Latinas Conference;  Latinas Leading the Future: Power, Influence, and Impact
description:
LUPE Fund, Inc's  "Power of Latinas: Strengthening Our Legacy," conference and networking reception will be held at Montclair State University's Hall  Conference Center  on October 1st, 2026. LUPE Fund, Inc., New Jersey's oldest Latina-run organization, proudly celebrated its 20th anniversary in 2023.  
 The Conference Center is located at Montclair State University Campus, at University Hall on the 7th Floor.  
 Join us for an inspiring and empowering event featuring panels in health & wellness, business, politics, and education. Each panelist is a powerful and influential Latina dedicated to making a difference. Refreshments will be available.

 2:00 PM - Registration Opens 3:00 PM - Opening Remarks 3:15 PM - Welcome Address 3:30 PM - Keynote Speaker -  Adel Wilson,  Assistant Secretary of State 4:00 PM - Panel 1 — Elección Latina: From Cultural Visibility to Civic Power 5:10 PM - Dinner Break 5:30 PM - Panel 2 — The Leadership Pipeline: Preparing Latinas to Lead the Next Economy 6:50 PM - Panel 3 — From Culture to Capital: Building Latina Economic Power 8:00 PM - Program Ends

title: Espresso Your Vote Grab a Coffee. Get Election Ready. (Montclair Campus)
description:
Start your day with coffee and conversation! Join the Office of Student Belonging and Civic and Voter Engagement for Espresso Your Vote, a welcoming pop-up event designed to help you prepare for the upcoming election. 
 Whether you need to register to vote, update your voter registration, check your registration status, or simply have questions about the voting process, our team is here to help. We'll provide trusted, nonpartisan information to ensure you have everything you need to vote with confidence. 
 Enjoy a complimentary cup of coffee while connecting with fellow students, learning about important election dates and deadlines, and discovering the many ways you can make your voice heard. 
 Stop by to: 
 
 Register to vote or update your voter registration 
 Verify your voter registration status 
 Learn about your voting options 
 Ask questions about the upcoming election 
 Grab a cup of coffee and connect with campus resources 
 
 Sometimes the best conversations happen over coffee. Take a break, enjoy a fresh cup, and leave feeling informed, prepared, and ready to participate in our democracy.

title: The American Experiment ;Migration, Identity, and the American Nation
description:
Join President Koppell for his first lecture in the American Experiment series, where he will discuss migration, identity, and the American nation. 
 Migration has been central to the American experience from the nation’s earliest history to the present. It has shaped the country’s population, economy, politics, culture, and understanding of national identity, while also generating recurring debates over citizenship, belonging, borders, assimilation, and exclusion. This lecture examines how migration, including internal and forced migration, has influenced the development of the United States and how Americans have defined who belongs within the national community. It considers the tensions between the country’s long-standing identity as a nation of immigrants and its equally significant history of restriction, exclusion, and contested membership. The discussion will explore how race, ethnicity, religion, class, and demographic change have shaped immigration policy and public attitudes, while placing contemporary debates over borders, citizenship, birthright citizenship, integration, and national identity within a broader historical and constitutional context. At its center is an enduring question for American democracy: How should a nation shaped by migration define membership, belonging, and shared identity in a period of rapid global and demographic change?

title: The Italian Job: Jason Horowitz in conversation with Mark Rotella
organization: College of Humanities and Social Sciences (CHSS)
location: School of Communication and Media, Presentation Hall
description:
Please complete this RSVP form to confirm your registration!   School of Communication and Media, Presentation Hall  Wednesday, Oct. 7 at 6:00pm 
 The  Coccia Institute  at Montclair State University welcomes New York Times Rome bureau correspondent Jason Horowitz to discuss The Italian Job with Coccia director  Mark Rotella . 
   
 From Venetian canals to Vatican conclaves, New York Times correspondent Jason Horowitz takes you on a tour of the real Italy. 
   
 Italy’s deep history, stunning landscapes and glorious food have uniquely captured our imagination. In The Italian Job, Jason Horowitz, a longtime Rome bureau chief for The New York Times, tells the story of how he too fell under that Tuscan-sun enchantment, before ultimately discovering a more fascinating Italy, a country conducting experiments in populist politics, confronting global challenges like immigration, climate change and an aging population. 
   
 Horowitz introduces us to an extraordinary range of characters. He flies with popes and drinks Spritzes with prime ministers, talks beauty with top fashion designers in Milan, ponders the big questions with cardinals in Rome, and gets his feet wet in the Venice lagoon with engineers trying to save the sinking city. Throughout, Italy’s streets, layered with history, and its cafés, vibrating with conversation, are full of lessons. So is his life at home, where his Italian wife and their two children offer an even more intimate, concentrated and rollicking view of Italian life. As years pass and the world turns upside down, Italy, more than a vacation destination or land of the past, reveals itself as a vivid lens through which to understand our present and future.

title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative
description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week.  
 To Participate : RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set! 
 Requirements: 
 
 Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate. 
 Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this   link . 
 Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate. 
 
 Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation! *Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: Faculty Concert: Chris Opperman, Composition
description:
Faculty Concert: Chris Opperman, Composition 
 Dr. Chris Opperman  wields a special array of expertise. He is a composer of wildly original music, a top orchestrator and arranger, a dedicated and visionary educator, and a trusted advisor for an incredible cross-section of the music industry. 
 Since starting his Purple Cow Records label in 1998, Dr. Opperman has released six prior albums including 2001’s Klavierstücke, his first solo piano album, and 2010’s The Lionheart, an orchestral rock album. He has also released three EP’s including 2022’s Four Improvisations which feature studio-manipulated piano works, and two singles including “And If You Know” featuring Robert Martin. 
 With Arnie & Eric Roth of AWR Music, Dr. Opperman has worked on several national and international orchestral and chamber music tours including Distant Worlds: music from FINAL FANTASY, A New World: intimate music from FINAL FANTASY, the FINAL FANTASY VII Remake Orchestra World Tour, The Beach Boys Holiday Vibrations Orchestra Tour, several Mannheim Steamroller Christmas tours, and Undertale LIVE. Dr. Opperman’s arrangements with AWR and others have been performed by renowned and accomplished orchestras at premiere venues which include Carnegie Hall, the Royal Albert Hall, the Tokyo International Forum, and more. 
 Along with much other music, Opperman played piano on two of Steve Vai’s Grammy-nominated compositions, “Lotus Feet” from Real Illusions: Reflections and “The Attitude Song” from Sound Theories, Vols. I and II, both with the Metropole Orkest. He’s also performed with virtuoso multi-instrumentalist Mike Keneally, Indian classical music masters L. Shankar (a.k.a. Shenkar) and Zakir Hussein, former Duran Duran/Missing Persons guitarist Warren Cuccurullo, and many others. 
 Dr. Opperman holds a Ph. D. In Music Composition and has taught undergraduate and graduate level courses on music theory and composition, popular and classical music history, music technology, and the music industry. 
 Learn more about Chris Opperman

description:
Coordinating with the release of the dam in the Lehigh River, this whitewater rafting trip is sure to be a blast. Perfect for all skill levels. This is a great way to GET YOUR FEET WET!  
   
 How do I Sign-up? 
 
 Register  here , or in the Student Recreation Center's main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340).

For warmer days, wear a swim suit or quick-drying shorts/shirt; for cooler days, bring extra layers, but no cotton. Wetsuits are included for those that want them. title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series
organization: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence
description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our  Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series , beginning  Monday, September 14 . 
 This  10-week workshop series  offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in  Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala  and are open to  students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University . No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. 
 Mondays, beginning September 14 5:30–7:30 p.m. Cole Hall, Room 141 10-week series 
 We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us.  Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

title: All In: The Fight for Democracy Film Screening & Civic Engagement Experience
description:
Democracy doesn't protect itself—it depends on informed, engaged citizens. 
 Join Civic and Voter Engagement, in collaboration with the African American Caucus, for a powerful screening of  All In: The Fight for Democracy , the critically acclaimed documentary that examines the history and present-day reality of voter suppression in the United States. Featuring voting rights advocate Stacey Abrams, the film explores the historical barriers, systemic inequities, and ongoing challenges that continue to shape access to the ballot box and influence civic participation. 
 More than a documentary, this screening is an opportunity to deepen your understanding of the democratic process, reflect on the importance of protecting voting rights, and engage in meaningful dialogue about one of the most fundamental rights in our democracy. 
 Following the screening, participants are invited to stay for a facilitated discussion exploring the themes of the film, the significance of voting rights in today's political landscape, and the role each of us can play in strengthening our democracy through civic engagement. Whether you're new to these conversations or actively engaged in public life, this discussion offers a welcoming space to learn from one another, share perspectives, and consider how informed civic participation can create positive change. 
 Join us for: 
 
 A screening of the award-winning documentary  All In: The Fight for Democracy 
 A facilitated discussion on the film's relevance to today's political climate 
 Meaningful conversation with fellow students, faculty, and staff 
 Free food and refreshments 
 Civic-themed giveaways 
 Resources to help you stay informed and engaged 
 
 This event is open to all students, faculty, and staff. Come for the film, stay for the conversation, and leave with a deeper understanding of the importance of civic participation and the power of every voice. 
 Good film. Great conversation. Free food. Giveaways. One important conversation about the future of our democracy.

title: AI Literacy for Educators
description: The AI literacy for educators designed to support educators in building a strong, practical understanding of artificial intelligence in educational contexts. This workshop will help educators understand foundational AI concepts, critically evaluate AI tools and outputs, recognize how bias and inequity can emerge in AI systems, and examine the ethical and societal implications of AI use in teaching and learning. title: New Jersey's 44th Annual Law School Day
description:
Are you thinking about applying to law school? Join us for our 44th Annual NJ Law School Day at Montclair State University! All NJ college students and alumni who are interested in applying to law school are welcome to attend! 
 At NJ Law School Day, you can speak with law school representatives from NJ, NY, and across the U.S. about what their programs have to offer and how you can prepare to be a strong law school candidate.  Whether you are new to the idea of applying to law school or preparing to apply this fall, this event is a great opportunity to learn and connect. 
 
   
 What to Expect from Law School Day : 
 1pm - 2pm - Law School Panel Discussion 
 - For this session, you will hear from a panel of law school representatives about what they look for when reviewing law school applications and how to become a strong law school candidate. 
   
 2 - 4pm - The Law School Fair 
 - This is your chance to meet face-to- face with law school representatives from NJ, NY, PA, MA and across the U.S., and ask questions about applying to law school! 
 - The list of law schools attending is growing! Current law schools attending include:  American, Fordham, Villanova, Ohio State, Seton Hall, Rutgers, Drexel, Penn State, Pace, Syracuse, Cardozo, Utah, Maryland, West Virginia, Richmond, Pittsburgh , and many, many more.   
 - You can see the full list of law schools attending once you RSVP on Handshake on or after September 1, 2026 
   
 3:30 - 4:30 PM - Speed Mentoring: Pathways to Public Service 
 -  After learning what it takes to get into law school, stick around to connect directly with professionals who are doing the work.   
 - Through fast-paced, small-group rotating conversations, you’ll discover real-world career paths, and get honest insights into public interest and public service work. Come listen, ask questions, grab a snack, and make connections that can kickstart your legal, public interest, or public service career. 
   
 How to Be Prepared for Law School Day : 
 
 Be ready to share information about you, your interests, and your goals! 
 Write down the questions you have about law schools and the process of applying to law school 
 Bring something to take notes 
 Dress to impress!  Business attire is recommended 
 Registration for Law School Day will open on September 1, 2026 on Handshake 
 Questions? Need law school advice? Email Chrysten Colacicco, Pre-Law Program Coordinator at MSU, at colaciccoc@montclair.edu

title: Speed Mentoring: Pathways to Public Service
description:
Join us for the grand finale of NJ  Law  School  Day ! 
 
 
 
 After learning what it takes to get into  law  school, stick around to connect directly with professionals who are doing the work. 
 This interactive session breaks away from traditional panels to give you direct access to public service professionals, legal practitioners, community advocates, legislative staff, policy experts, and elected officials. 
 Through fast-paced, small-group rotating conversations, you’ll discover real-world career paths, and get honest insights into public interest work. Come listen, ask questions, grab a snack, and make connections that can kickstart your legal or public service career. 
 
 
 
 
 Questions?  Contact Donna Robertson at  chsscareer@montclair.edu .

title: Campus Walking Challenge
description:
Let’s walk and roll this fall!  Join the Department of Kinesiology, the Exercise Science Student Organization, and Athletics & Recreation as we take part in the Exercise is Medicine - On Campus walking challenge.  Our goal is to accumulate as many miles as we can during these 8 hours by encouraging physical activity in a friendly competition against other universities. You can track your steps/miles using your phone and submit them virtually and earn bonus miles by changing up your campus commute routine by visiting the following link and logging your steps:  https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScnl5q0PKYQDVTEZp67DCAD4974cJcFB07IWkNMnkCc-CEvSA/viewform?usp=dialog

title: ACC Teach-In: On the Origins of Modern US Foreign Interventionism & Iran
description: Drawing inspiration from the mid-1960s anti-war movement, this teach-in will be an action-based educational forum concerning modern US foreign interventionism and its historical convergence with Iran during the Cold War. More specifically, it will focus on the rise of the postwar national security state and its first pivotal and consequential “win”: the 1953 Iranian coup d'état. It was the first "successful" overthrow of a democratically elected foreign leader by the CIA (and definitely not the last). It is a tale that is regularly expunged from conventional American history, yet it is vastly significant to both Iranian US history. This chapter elucidates, in part, why both nations find themselves where they are today. In addition, this teach-in will also highlight the determining role of big business, military keynesianism, and neocolonialism in shaping the confines of postwar U.S. foreign policy. This teach-in will conclude with a discussion on what this all means for the ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran, and what actionable acts can be done to end the conflict.

title: Week of Wisdom: Bloom Bar with the Cussies
organization: Chi Upsilon Sigma National Latin Sorority, INC
description: Join the Cussies for Bloom Bar, a meaningful evening focused on self-love, finding your voice, and raising awareness about domestic violence. Together, we'll create a safe and supportive space for reflection, open conversation, and empowerment while reminding one another of the importance of healing, advocacy, and community. During the event, each attendee will create a personalized bouquet of three roses, with each rose symbolizing a powerful reminder to carry with them: love, strength, and resilience. We hope you'll leave with not only a beautiful bouquet, but also a meaningful reminder of your value, your strength, and your ability to continue blooming.

title: New Hope Garden Trip
description:
Join us to visit Bowman's Hill Wildflower Preserve and explore over 130 acres of beautiful native plants, peaceful woodland trails, and scenic outdoor views perfect for a relaxing day in nature.  Optional add on : The New Hope Railroad (starting at $35) for a charming rail ride through the Pennsylvania countryside or explore the town of New Hope. Tickets for the railroad are not covered by Outdoor Adventure, and must be purchased on your own. 
   
 How do I sign-up? 
 
 Register  here  or in the Student Rec Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). 
 Cost for Students $10 
 
   
 Where and when? 
 
 October 17th, 2026 
 9am-6pm 
 Bus leaves from Student Recreation Center 
 
   
 What to bring:  Bring lunch, water, sneakers and a sense of adventure!  
   
 Potential Hazards:  Unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, dehydration, allergic reactions/poisonous plants, insect bites, and injury by running, including sprains, lacerations, abrasions and fractures.

title: Free Swim Lessons *Beginner*
description:
Never swam before? No problem! These lessons will give you the important foundational skills in swimming and help you be more comfortable in the pool. Learn how to use proper breath control, float, and swim with a kickboard.  
   
 Skills Focus: 
 
 Being comfortable in the water 
 Learning how to float on your back and front 
 Learning how to kick off the wall with a kickboard 
 Introducing proper breath control in the water 
 Learning how to tread water 
 Learn alternate kicks (Froggy Kick) 
 Being comfortable in the deep end  
 Introducing arms to your strokes 
 
 
 How do I Sign-up? 
 
 Registration is not required 
 FREE with a valid Montclair State ID 
 
   
 When and Where? 
 
 Student Recreation Center - Pool

title: What is a Man?
organization: Lambda Sigma Upsilon Latino Fraternity, Inc.
description: What is a Man? is a real and open dialogue centered on the stigmatization of men and the expectations placed on masculinity. This space explores how societal pressures often force men to suppress emotion, struggle in silence, and avoid vulnerability. Through honest conversation, we aim to break down those barriers and address men’s mental health in a meaningful way. It’s a judgment-free environment that encourages reflection, healing, and connection, reminding everyone that redefining strength starts with being able to speak, feel, and be heard.

description: Join us for the Native African Student Organization's General Body Meeting! This is a space where we come together to celebrate and explore the richness of African cultures, while also connecting with other cultures from around the world. At each meeting, we'll engage in lively discussions, learn about Africa’s diverse history, traditions, and current events, and empower each other to understand and embrace our heritage. Whether you're looking to deepen your cultural knowledge, make meaningful connections, or simply have fun with fellow students who share a passion for Africa and global cultures, this is the place to be! Let’s build a supportive community, amplify African voices on campus, and create lasting friendships. All are welcome, come, learn, share, and connect!

title: Free Swim Lessons *Intermediate*
description:
Take your swimming to the next level! Get introduced to new strokes or work on the ones you already know. These lessons are for swimmers who are a little more comfortable in the water but still want to improve their technique and expand what skills they know.  
   
 Skills Focus: 
 
 Swimming unassisted on your front and back  
 Improve treading (in the deep end) 
 Improving breath control in the water 
 Learn alternate kicks (Dolphin Kick) 
 Introduction to and/or improving your breaststroke 
 Swimming laps 
 Introduction to open and flip turns 
 Introduction to Butterfly 
 
   
 How do I Sign-up? 
 
 Registration is not required 
 FREE with a valid Montclair State ID 
 
   
 When and Where? 
 Student Rec Center - Pool

title: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People Weekly Discussion
organization: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People
location: University Hall 1020 - Bard-Blount Family Lecture Hall
description:
Welcome Back! 
 Our weekly NAACP discussion space is dedicated to education, empowerment, and collective action. Each Monday from 2:00 PM – 3:15 PM, we gather to engage in meaningful conversations surrounding civil rights, social justice, advocacy, and current events impacting Black communities on campus and beyond. 
 Each week brings something new — current events, culture, advocacy topics, campus concerns, or whatever’s on our minds. Come through, share your voice, and be part of a community that’s always growing and always pushing forward.

location: Bloomfield - Talbott Hall TM04 - Room of Excellence
description:
Greek Council Meetings are held bi-weekly on Mondays from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM and bring together recognized Greek organizations and fellowships to discuss important updates, upcoming events, initiatives, responsibilities, and matters impacting the Greek community. 
 These meetings are exclusively for members and representatives of recognized Greek organizations and fellowships. They are not open to the general student body or non-Greek attendees. 
 Organizations and fellowships are encouraged to have representation at each meeting to stay informed and engaged with Greek Council.

title: The Big 3 Competition
description:
The big 3 lifts (Deadlift, Squat, and Bench Press) are the foundation of true strength, and now it is your time to dominate the platform. Whether you’re lifting for the glory, the prizes, or just to beat your PR this is your chance to push your limits and have fun, all while getting to utilize our brand new strength equipment! 
   
 
 How are results scored? 
 
 Maximum 5 repetitions 
 1 attempt per lift after a warm-up set 
 Scoring calculation: Weight lifted x repetitions divided by body weight 
 Final score will be total of 3 lifts combined

description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our  Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series , beginning  Monday, September 14 . 
 This  10-week workshop series  offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in  Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala  and are open to  students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University . No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. 
 Mondays, beginning September 14 5:30–7:30 p.m. Cole Hall, Room 141 10-week series 
 We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us.  Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

title: Graduate and Health Professions School Fair 2026
description:
Are you pursuing a career that requires a graduate or professional degree? Do you need help planning your next steps after graduation? 
 Join us for the Graduate and Health Professions School Fair to meet admission representatives from both graduate and health profession schools!   The Pre-Medical Program and The Office for Experiential Education and Career Connections invite students of all levels and majors to connect with admissions representatives in a wide variety of fields! Students can also attend professional development and admission preparation workshops during the fair. 
 More Information: 
   
 
 Free to attend for all Montclair and Bloomfield campus students and alums. 
 Come prepared with questions to ask each school representative. 
 Bring plenty of copies of your resume. 
 Workshops on professional development and tips for the admissions process will be offered during the fair. 
 Students must bring their Montclair State University Student IDs. 
 Registration is required through Handshake. 
 Students who attend will receive giveaways. 
 Professional attire is highly encouraged. 
 The proceeds from this fair allow the Pre-Medical Program to provide free admissions test preparation resources to our pre-med and pre-health students! 
 
 Event details: 
 
 Graduation and Health Professions School Fair
 
 Location: University Hall, 7th Floor (Conference Center) 
 Time: 12 PM - 3 PM

organization: The Office for Experiential Education and Career Connections
description:
Join alumni from the College of the Arts as they share their career journeys, discuss how they transitioned from college to the professional world, and offer advice for students interested in creative careers. 
 Panelists will discuss: 
 
 Building a career in the arts and creative industries 
 Navigating internships, auditions, and professional opportunities 
 Developing industry connections and professional networks 
 Skills that helped them succeed after graduation 
 Challenges, opportunities, and lessons learned along the way 
 
 Featured career areas include: 
 
 Performing Arts and Theater Production 
 Fashion and Apparel 
 Dance and Performance 
 Arts Administration 
 Human Resources in Creative Industries 
 
 Students will have the opportunity to ask questions, learn about different career paths, and gain firsthand insights from CART alumni who have successfully launched their careers.

title: Day at the Capitol - Fall 2026
description:
Take your voice beyond campus! 
 Join us for a Day in the Capitol , a chance to sit in on state committee hearings, hear real testimony, and see the democratic process in action. You’ll tour the NJ State Capitol, connect with legislators, and advocate for your community. The best part? It’s all FREE (transportation + lunch included)! 
 Network with like-minded professionals, engage in politics, and develop a new perspective on the legislative process. 
 Don’t just learn about change… be part of it. 
 📍 Transportation will be provided from the Red Hawk Deck on College Ave, Montclair, NJ, 07043 and from Bloomfield Campus

title: Roll Up a Sleeve, Save a Life! - Blood Drive
location: Student Center Ballrooms B/C  1 Normal Avenue , Upper Montclair, New Jersey
description:
Calling all Montclair State faculty, staff, and students—it’s time to be a hero! Join us for our  Blood Drive  in proud partnership with the  American Red Cross  and help make a life-saving impact. Whether you’re a first-time donor or a seasoned pro, your donation can help replenish critical blood supplies used in emergencies, surgeries, and more. It’s quick, easy, and one of the most meaningful ways to give back to your community. 
 So roll up your sleeve, grab a friend, and join us in turning compassion into action—because  every drop counts . Snacks, smiles, and gratitude await!  
 RSVPing on Engage does not mean you are registered to donate. You must click and follow the link below in order to register as a donor for the drive! 
 https://www.redcrossblood.org/give.html/drive-results?zipSponsor=Redhawk

title: Learning in Circle: English for the Community
organization: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence
description:
CLaSE invites members of the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in  Learning in Circle: English for the Community , beginning  Thursday, September 17 . 
 This  10-week workshop series  provides a welcoming and supportive environment for adult learners who want to strengthen their  English conversation and comprehension skills  through practical, interactive activities. Workshops are open to  students, families, and community members from outside the University . 
 Thursdays, beginning September 17 6–7:30 p.m. Schmitt Hall, Room 104 10-week series 
 The workshops are  free and open to the community , but  registration is required by contacting calarotaa@montclair.edu . We invite anyone interested in improving their English skills to join us and learn in community!

description:

title: DECA General Body Meeting
location: School Of Business 140 - James Merli Executive Education Conference Room
description:
Join us for our General Body Meetings throughout the semester! Whether you're a returning member or brand new to DECA, our GBMs are the perfect place to stay connected, meet fellow students, hear about upcoming events, competitions, professional development opportunities, networking experiences, and ways to get involved. Come build your leadership skills, grow your network, and make the most of your DECA experience. We can't wait to see you there! 
 This month, we're putting the spotlight on  Sports Business!  🏆 We'll explore all things DECA-related to the sports industry, including marketing, management, hospitality, sales, entrepreneurship, and more, while preparing for our  DECA @ Devils game . Come learn, connect, and get ready to take DECA to the next level!

title: Check In, Not Out
organization: Sigma Lambda Beta International Fraternity Inc.
description: Check In, Not Out is a mental health awareness tabling event designed to promote wellness, reduce stigma, and connect students with valuable mental health resources.  T o learn practical self-care strategies, participate in interactive activities, and explore campus support services. Attendees will have the opportunity to engage in meaningful conversations about mental health in a welcoming and inclusive environment. Stop by to take a break, grab helpful resources, and prioritize your well-being.

title: SLAM General Body Meeting
description: Come hang out with the SLAM E-Board and get involved in shaping our events for the semester! Our Bi-Weekly General Body Meetings are a space for students to learn about upcoming programs, share ideas, and help plan and execute events that bring the campus together. Whether you’re interested in event planning, marketing, logistics, or just want your voice heard, this is the place to be. We’ll be discussing what’s ahead for the semester, ways to get involved, and how you can make a real impact through SLAM. No experience is needed—just bring your ideas, energy, and excitement to collaborate with us!

title: Common Errors for Multilingual Writers
description: Whether you're in the process of learning English or if English is not your native tongue, there are common writing errors that you will find in your writing. This workshop reviews the grammar rules for some of the most common errors made by multilingual writers. Join us to review strategies for catching preposition usage mistakes and more.

organization: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People
location: University Hall 1020 - Bard-Blount Family Lecture Hall
description:
Welcome Back! 
 Our weekly NAACP discussion space is dedicated to education, empowerment, and collective action. Each Monday from 2:00 PM – 3:15 PM, we gather to engage in meaningful conversations surrounding civil rights, social justice, advocacy, and current events impacting Black communities on campus and beyond. 
 Each week brings something new — current events, culture, advocacy topics, campus concerns, or whatever’s on our minds. Come through, share your voice, and be part of a community that’s always growing and always pushing forward.

LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our  Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series , beginning  Monday, September 14 . 
 This  10-week workshop series  offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in  Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala  and are open to  students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University . No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. 
 Mondays, beginning September 14 5:30–7:30 p.m. Cole Hall, Room 141 10-week series 
 We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us.  Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

title: The American Experiment: Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment
description:
Join President Koppell for his first lecture in the American Experiment series, where he will discuss Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment. 
 The First Amendment is the cornerstone of American democracy because it guarantees the fundamental freedoms required for citizens to govern themselves, including freedom of speech, freedom of the press, and freedom of assembly.  Citizens need access to open debate, diverse viewpoints, and accurate information in order to make informed decisions. These freedoms also protect unpopular and minority opinions and act as a check on the state from censoring speech or controlling what people learn, think, and say.  This lecture examines the foundational freedoms of the First Amendment and how they are applied to contemporary American democratic life, including: the impact of money on expression, the role of new media and corporate media, the role of the press in investigating and disseminating information, the right to protest as a form of assembly and expression, and the challenges posed by misinformation, disinformation, polarization, fragmented media audiences, and declining public trust. At its center is a fundamental question for American democracy: What are the inherent rights and responsibilities of freedom of expression in a democratic society?

title: Midterms Election Watch Party, Pizza & Power: Watch Democracy Unfold Live!
description:
Join us for an exciting Midterm Election Night Party on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, from 7 to 10 p.m. in the Fish Bowl, located in the School of Communication and Media lobby! 
 Come together with members of the campus community to watch the midterm election results unfold in real time. Follow the action and see who will prevail in New Jersey’s 12 U.S. House of Representatives districts, while also keeping an eye on other key races from across the country. 
 Hosted by the Office of Civic and Voter Engagement, the Department of Political Science and Law, the Political Science Club, and the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, the event will offer a lively and welcoming space to discuss the races, exchange insights, and experience democracy in action. 
 Whether you closely follow politics or simply want to enjoy the excitement of Election Night, this is a great opportunity to connect with others over pizza, conversation, and live results. Bring your friends and join us for an engaging evening as the nation decides the makeup of the next Congress!

title: Accounting Society - Wiss & Company
description: Wiss & Company LLP is a top 100 U.S. accounting and advisory firm founded in 1969. Headquartered in Florham Park, New Jersey, the firm operates additional offices in Flemington, New York City, and Boca Raton. Under the leadership of CEO Paul Peterson, a specialized team of roughly 450 employees serves middle-market businesses and private clients. Their comprehensive services include full-scale accounting, audit assurance, strategic tax planning, and outsourced fractional CFO solutions. Furthermore, Wiss Private Client Advisors delivers specialized wealth management and estate planning services. Finally, the firm drives business modernization through targeted process automation and AI-driven data intelligence.

title: Hillel Hang
description:
Shalom Red Hawks, 
 Hillel Hang is a weekly, low-key gathering where students can come together, relax, get some homework done, grab snacks, and spend time with friends. title: 1st International Symposium of Latino Oral History
organization: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence
description:
Join us for the  First International Symposium of Latino Oral History, “Listening as Resistance: Oral History, Memory and the Latino Experience”  taking place virtually on  November 6–7 . This two-day symposium will bring together scholars, students, educators, writers, and community members to explore the power of  oral history and Latino storytelling  as tools for preserving lived experiences, amplifying voices, and challenging dominant historical narratives. 
 We are honored to welcome acclaimed  writer, journalist, and University of California, Irvine professor Héctor Tobar  as our keynote speaker. 
 We invite participants to  submit an abstract  to present their work or  register to attend  and learn more about Latino storytelling and oral history practices. 
 Best paper will get a chance to be published in an academic journal. 
 Student registration is free. 
 Please register for the symposium with the link below: 
 https://montclair.co1. qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ cYowQOHwct2em0K 
 To submit an abstract:  
  https://montclair.co1. qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ 1N6j22Uqp6ulqiq

title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series
organization: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence
description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our  Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series , beginning  Monday, September 14 . 
 This  10-week workshop series  offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in  Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala  and are open to  students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University . No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. 
 Mondays, beginning September 14 5:30–7:30 p.m. Cole Hall, Room 141 10-week series 
 We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us.  Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

title: Accounting Society - Nisivoccia
description: Nisivoccia LLP  is a prominent accounting, tax, and advisory firm founded in 1964 and based in New Jersey. Led by Managing Partner Nick Sarinelli, the firm operates out of offices including Mount Arlington, Bridgewater, and Newton. Their 140+ professionals provide financial statement audits, year-round tax planning, and strategic business advisory services. They specialize heavily in serving not-for-profit organizations, school districts, governmental bodies, and commercial real estate clients. Additionally, the firm offers specialized divisions for IT consulting, cybersecurity, and forensic fraud accounting. Over its 60-year history, Nisivoccia LLP has grown into a highly trusted regional partner for private and public entities.

description: Join All Pockets Full for our in-person General Body Meeting at Montclair State University. This meeting is an opportunity to connect with other students who are interested in business, finance, entrepreneurship, personal growth, and building a stronger future. We’ll have real conversations, interactive discussions, and activities designed to help you learn, connect, and grow. title: NASO General Body Meeting
description: Join us for the Native African Student Organization's General Body Meeting! This is a space where we come together to celebrate and explore the richness of African cultures, while also connecting with other cultures from around the world. At each meeting, we'll engage in lively discussions, learn about Africa’s diverse history, traditions, and current events, and empower each other to understand and embrace our heritage. Whether you're looking to deepen your cultural knowledge, make meaningful connections, or simply have fun with fellow students who share a passion for Africa and global cultures, this is the place to be! Let’s build a supportive community, amplify African voices on campus, and create lasting friendships. All are welcome, come, learn, share, and connect!

title: Find the Sources You Need
description:
Learn where and how to search for books, articles, and more.  We’ll break down the differences between primary and secondary sources.  We'll discuss "credible sources," both those from scholarly (peer-reviewed) journals and those from other sources.  We'll also discuss, among other things, the differences between our two largest family of databases -- ProQuest and EBSCO. title: Cali Immersive Residency: The Hands Free & Dance Heginbotham —The Party Scene
description:
Exquisitely eclectic quartet  The Hands Free  and members of the fabulously whimsical  Dance Heginbotham  join forces in  The Party Scene . Inspired by  The Nutcracker  and your holiday office party, this music and dance extravaganza is part Drosselmeyer and part Turkey Lurkey Time. Lightly immersive and family-friendly, The Party Scene features student party guests from Montclair State University. All guests are encouraged to don impressively festive seasonal sweaters. 
 About The Hands Free:  The Hands Free is an acoustic quartet, bringing together the creative voices of composer/performers  James Moore  (guitar & banjo),  Caroline Shaw  (violin),  Nathan Koci  (accordion), and  Eleonore Oppenheim  (bass). Drawing from an eclectic array of influences in classical, jazz, and folk traditions, the group produces a unique and evocative blend of joyful melodies, lush sonic textures, and explosive improvisations. 
 About Dance Heginbotham:  Dance Heginbotham (DH) is a New York-based contemporary dance company committed to supporting, producing, and performing the work of choreographer  John Heginbotham . With an emphasis on collaboration, DH enriches national and international communities through its unique blend of inventive, thoughtful, and rigorous dance-theater works. Founded in 2011, DH had its world premiere in January 2012 at  The Kennedy Center  and has been presented by major venues throughout the US, including  Bard SummerScape, Brooklyn Academy of Music, Hopkins Center for the Arts, Jacob’s Pillow Dance Festival, The Joyce Theater, Lincoln Center, The Metropolitan Museum of Art,  and  Works Process at The Guggenheim,  among many others. DH has shared the stage with luminaries of the music world, including  Alarm Will Sound, Brooklyn Rider, The Knights, National Symphony Orchestra, Joshua Bell, André de Ridder,  and  Eric Jacobsen,  and has commissioned new scores from composers  Tyondai Braxton, Ethan Iverson,  and  Colin Jacobsen.  DH has collaborated with designers and artists  Maira Kalman, Isaac Mizrahi, Amy Trompetter, Maile Okamura,  and  Nicole Pearce i n the creation of new works. 
 www.danceheginbotham.org   
 Learn more about the Cali Immersive Residency Program at Montclair's Cali School of Music

title: NASO General Body Meeting
description: Join us for the Native African Student Organization's General Body Meeting! This is a space where we come together to celebrate and explore the richness of African cultures, while also connecting with other cultures from around the world. At each meeting, we'll engage in lively discussions, learn about Africa’s diverse history, traditions, and current events, and empower each other to understand and embrace our heritage. Whether you're looking to deepen your cultural knowledge, make meaningful connections, or simply have fun with fellow students who share a passion for Africa and global cultures, this is the place to be! Let’s build a supportive community, amplify African voices on campus, and create lasting friendships. All are welcome, come, learn, share, and connect!

title: Canva Masterclass: Advanced Tools & Pro Design Hacks
description: Ready to level up your Canva skills? This advanced workshop dives into powerful features like animations, brand kits, collaboration tools, and interactive content creation. title: Accounting Society - KPMG
description: KPMG is a prominent global network of independent firms delivering professional audit, tax, and advisory services. As one of the prestigious "Big Four" accounting firms, it operates across roughly 140 countries and employs over 270,000 professionals worldwide. The organization was officially formed in 1987 through the merger of Peat Marwick International and Klynveld Main Goerdeler, with its name representing the initials of its foundational partners. Instead of functioning as a single multinational corporation, KPMG is structured as a network of distinct, locally managed member firms. Its primary client base includes major corporations, government agencies, and non-profit institutions seeking regulatory compliance and strategic business consulting. Through this decentralized model, the firm maintains a massive footprint in global financial compliance and corporate restructuring.

title: Chamber Opera Performance: "L'enfant et les Sortilèges"
description:
Maurice Ravel ’s  L’enfant et les sortilèges  is a wildly imaginative fantasy opera where a single child’s tantrum sets an entire enchanted world into motion. In a flash of frustration, the ordinary becomes extraordinary—walls start to whisper, teacups burst into song, animals argue back, and the child’s room transforms into a living, breathing world of magic and mischief. 
 As this fantastical realm awakens, the child is swept into a dazzling swirl of musical surprises and unexpected voices, where every object has something to say and nothing is quite as it seems. With Ravel’s shimmering, kaleidoscopic score at its heart, this enchanting opera is a playful journey through wonder, chaos, and the power of imagination to transform everything it touches. 
 (Sung in French with English Surtitles~ runtime: approx 1 hour) 
 Montclair State University Students  FREE  with ID at Kasser Box Office

title: Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers with New Jersey Hall of Fame
description:
Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers invites educators to explore how the powerful, personal stories of New Jersey Hall of Fame inductees can serve as catalysts for meaningful social-emotional learning and authentic civic engagement in today’s classrooms. By examining moments of courage, empathy, advocacy, and ethical decision-making in the lives of New Jersey leaders, educators will uncover practical ways to help students build self-awareness, social awareness, and a sense of agency. 
 Drawing from the lives and legacies of Peter J. McGuire (Father of Labor Day), Dorothea Dix (mental health reformer), David Mixner (political activist, author, and playwright), and Clara Maass (public health pioneer), participants will analyze how these changemakers confronted injustice, advocated for vulnerable communities, and took action in times of social and public health crises—making abstract concepts such as fairness, wellness, and justice tangible and relevant for students.  
 Educators will compare and contrast AI-powered lesson generators, including MagicSchool and Curipod, and create SEL or civic action lessons and student activities using inductee stories, leveraging AI scaffolding to differentiate instruction for diverse learners. This workshop empowers educators to transform local legends into catalysts for empathy, critical thinking, and civic participation—helping all students see themselves as the next generation of changemakers.

 We'll begin with a special  flag raising ceremony at 12:30 PM in the Student Center Flag Pole  to collectively lift up the trailblazing women who have paved the way for us all.

 This is your chance to celebrate, connect, and show some serious school spirit. Bring your energy, bring your pride, and get ready for an unforgettable afternoon! 
   
 Tell a friend to tell a friend. We can't wait to see you there!

title: "Phaedra" by Elizabeth Egloff
description:
Written by  Elizabeth Egloff  | Directed by  Debbie Saivetz 
 Set in a timeless, surreal Mediterranean landscape, "Phaedra" by Elizabeth Egloff is a reimagining of the classical myth that shifts the focus from grand public tragedy to a deeply personal experience of solitude, longing, and memory. The story is told by a mysterious Narrator who is haunted by the memory of Phaedra, a Queen paralyzed by a forbidden passion for her stepson, Hippolytus. As Phaedra languishes on her daybed, attended by her Nurse and observed by a chatty, opinionated Chorus, the world around her takes on a dreamlike quality where a sewing machine clatters with the rhythm of a heart and the landscape is an itemization of blue, leaving every character adrift in a sea of unrequited memory. When Phaedra finally breaks her silence to confront Hippolytus, her confession leads not to connection but to a psychic "emptying" of herself. The play concludes with the Narrator left in his own solitude, haunted by the echoes of those who have passed away. 
 
 Montclair State University Students:  FREE  tickets with ID at Kasser Box Office

 Set in a timeless, surreal Mediterranean landscape, "Phaedra" by Elizabeth Egloff is a reimagining of the classical myth that shifts the focus from grand public tragedy to a deeply personal experience of solitude, longing, and memory. The story is told by a mysterious Narrator who is haunted by the memory of Phaedra, a Queen paralyzed by a forbidden passion for her stepson, Hippolytus. As Phaedra languishes on her daybed, attended by her Nurse and observed by a chatty, opinionated Chorus, the world around her takes on a dreamlike quality where a sewing machine clatters with the rhythm of a heart and the landscape is an itemization of blue, leaving every character adrift in a sea of unrequited memory. When Phaedra finally breaks her silence to confront Hippolytus, her confession leads not to connection but to a psychic "emptying" of herself. The play concludes with the Narrator left in his own solitude, haunted by the echoes of those who have passed away. 
 
 Montclair State University Students:  FREE  tickets with ID at Kasser Box Office

title: Denim Day: Mind the Gaps, Move Forward
description:
April is Sexual Assault Awareness Month, and together, we can break the silence.  The Montclair State University Police Department and the Office of Advocacy & Outreach are committed to fostering a campus where survivors feel heard, supported, and empowered.  It starts with believing. It starts with you.  By offering a safe and affirming response to those who disclose gender-based and sexual violence, we can create lasting change. Let’s stand together to end the cycle of silence—because  every voice matters, and every action counts. 
 Denim Day is recognized internationally as a day of action and awareness, encouraging people to wear denim to challenge victim-blaming and educate others about sexual violence.  This year, Denim Day falls on Wednesday, April 28, 2027. 
 The University Police and  Office of Advocacy & Outreach and the Office of Advocacy and Community Resilience , in partnership with over 30 campus and local community organizations, invites you to join us  from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. at the Amphitheater  for a powerful awareness event honoring survivors and increasing awareness of available resources. 
 Despite the  gaps  that still exist in the criminal justice system, in resources, and in prevention education,  we will move forward together  as a community. As part of this commitment, we will walk  one mile around campus in solidarity with survivors.
